events.text: In the deep they still tell it as a warning: a daughter of the Dragon King went up by a well and kept a house, and came back with her hair smelling of smoke. You have held rain over three provinces and you have never once seen anyone drink it. You find you would like to. A well is only a very narrow river, standing on end, and you know a shape that would fit.

choices.text: Go up one, in the blue hour, in a person's shape

effects.log: You come out on the wet stones perfectly dry, and that is your first mistake. Nobody is about. You stand holding the rim, and the air has a great many smells in it, and most of them are breakfast.

choices.text: No. Those who go up come back smelling of smoke

effects.log: You stay down, where you are owed things. The rain goes out on time that spring. It has never occurred to anyone to thank it, and it does not occur to you to mind.

events.text: A village well, before light. A person comes for water with two buckets on a yoke, walking as if the whole road had been laid on one shoulder. You watch the rope come up, hand over hand. You have moved rivers from one county to the next by being annoyed. You had not known that it weighed anything. They slop a little on the stones, and they look at that, and they say a short hard word.

choices.text: Wet your hand, and lift a bucket yourself to see

effects.log: It is absurd. It pulls your arm down out of the shoulder. You carry it four steps before you set it down, shaking, and a thing with a thousand years on it has learned something from a pail.

choices.text: Go back down. It is hardly your affair how they fetch it

effects.log: You go back down. For some reason you send that village a very good rain in the sowing month, and you tell yourself that it was on the way.

events.text: At a dry well in the south they are queuing with numbered pebbles. You have never stood in a line. You walk to the front of it in your good dry clothes and lean over, to see what the matter is. A great many people explain it to you. One of them is about ninety. She holds up her pebble, which is a forty-one, and asks you who you think you are.

choices.text: Go to the back, and get a pebble

effects.log: You wait there for most of a day, in the sun. It is a new idea, and you do not like it. You reach the rim at dusk with a borrowed gourd, and the water is brown, and you drink it. So that is what it is for.

choices.text: Tell her. You are feeling truthful

effects.log: She laughs so hard that she has to sit down. Forty people hear about it. You leave by the road, as quickly as a person can, and the water in that well comes up by a span, out of pure temper.

events.text: The rains are late this year and a county has built you. It is straw, about as long as a barn, and it has a very stupid face. They carry it to the pool, and then they beat it, and shout that it is lazy, and they throw dirt in your water, and the old men take turns telling it what they think. You stand at the back of the crowd in your shape. It is all quite sincere, and you have rarely been so insulted.

choices.text: Rain on them. Hard, and a little to the left of the crops

effects.log: They cheer. They carry the thing home in the wet, very pleased with the beating, and they will do it just the same next time. You see now how you have been managed.

choices.text: Help carry it, and find out what they say when it is over

effects.log: They give you a stick. What they say, when it is over, is that it is a hard year, and that the straw will do for thatch. Nobody here thinks that anyone is coming, and they did it anyway.

events.text: Every spring someone has to go down the village well and scrub it, and this year you are in it. {npc} comes down the ladder backwards with a brush in {his} teeth and stops with one foot on your shoulder. {He} takes the brush out. {He} looks at your sleeves. "Nobody is dry in a well," {he} says. "I have been in every one in this county, and I would know. Hold the lamp, if you are staying."

choices.text: Hold the lamp

effects.log: You hold it for most of a morning, very badly. {He} scrubs, and tells you what is wrong with the village, and asks you nothing further. You have not been given an order in eight hundred years. You keep the lamp quite level.

choices.text: Be gone by the time {he} looks round

effects.log: {He} looks round, and looks up, and looks down, and {he} goes on scrubbing. That is all. In the next few springs that well is scrubbed by someone who does not talk, and you notice that you know.

events.text: You have started to turn up. {npc} has four wells to see to in the east of the county, and you come along and carry the brushes, because {he} gave them to you once and did not take them back. At the third well {he} sits down on the rim, and pours a dipper of it over {his} own head, and groans with joy. You look at this for some time. "What?" {he} says. You ask what that is like.

choices.text: Let {him} pour one over you, and try to feel it

effects.log: It runs down your neck. You are not thirsty, and you are not hot, and you have never been either. {He} watches your face and starts to laugh. "Oh, you poor thing," {he} says, and {he} means it, and nobody has ever said that to you.

choices.text: Tell {him} that you know a good deal about water

effects.log: "Do you," says {npc}, and hands you the bucket, and points at the hill. You are out of breath at the top. You did not know you could be. You stand up there with the bucket and the view, knowing a good deal about water.

events.text: {npc} has an aunt, who wants a look at you. The aunt has you sit down on the good mat and begins. What are your people? "In the east," you say. And what do they do there? You think about that. "Rain," you say. There is a silence in the room. "Water trade," says {npc} quickly, chewing. The aunt looks at your hands, which have never done anything, and asks how much of it you own.

choices.text: Say that you own none of it. That is true, and it is a relief

effects.log: The aunt nods slowly. It is the first sensible thing heard from anyone of that age. You are given the burnt part of the rice, which you are told, later, is a great honour in that house.

choices.text: Tell the aunt all three provinces, and let it lie where it falls

effects.log: "Hm," says the aunt. The aunt has heard that from a salt merchant, and knows what became of the merchant. {npc} kicks you, and you are very much surprised. It is the first time anything has got through.

events.text: It is the day before, on the rim of the old well, and you had better say it. You go home by the well. You have to. And when you go, you cannot be watched: it is not a rule that you made, it is very old, and whoever looks has lost you. {npc} scratches {his} jaw with the brush. "How long does it take?" {he} says. You do not know. Nobody has ever asked. You say about a hundred.

choices.text: Ask it. "Turn your back, and count, and I will come back"

effects.log: {He} holds out {his} wet hand on it, as you would on the price of a pig. So it is done, with a bow to the aunt and a bad meal. On the fifth evening you go to the well, and behind you, not very well, somebody starts to count.

choices.text: You cannot ask that of anyone. Take back the question

effects.log: You say that it was a foolish idea. {He} looks at you for some time. "It was not," {he} says. "But you go on home." You go down that night, and {he} does not turn around, and it does not matter.

events.text: You do not sweat. In the sixth month, when the whole village lies flat on the floor with its mouth open, {npc} comes in from the third well and puts {his} forehead on your arm. {He} stays there. "You are the only cold thing in this province," {he} says, with {his} eyes shut, "and I want it known that this is why." Outside the rice is standing in hot water and everything smells of it.

choices.text: Hold still until {he} sleeps

effects.log: You stay for the night, with your arm gone dead. You did not know that arms did that. You could have this whole county in cool rain by morning, and you do not move, because {he} would wake.

choices.text: Send the rain, then, for everybody

effects.log: It comes up at midnight, all across the county. People go out and stand in it. {npc} wakes and looks at the roof, and looks at you, and {he} says that you might have asked, because the peppers were out.

events.text: Every fifth evening you go to the yard well, and {npc} turns {his} back and counts, out loud, like a person doing accounts. {He} is a poor counter. {He} goes wrong around sixty, and goes back. You hear it get smaller as you go down, and you are home with your whole length in the cold when you notice that you can still hear it. {He} is still up there in the dark, at eighty-something. It was only a bargain.

choices.text: Stay under the rim, this once, until {he} finishes

effects.log: Ninety-eight. Ninety-nine. {He} takes a moment over the last one, as you do with the last of a good meal, and you hear {his} feet go in. It is a long way to the sea from there, and you are late for a storm.

choices.text: Go on down. There is a storm owed in the south

effects.log: The storm goes out on time. Its timing is perfect. In the middle of it, over somebody's barley, you catch yourself thinking: sixty-one, sixty-two, no, wait.

events.text: It is a dry year for everyone but your yard. The well goes on, sweet and full, and by the second month there is a line at the gate with their pebbles. {npc} gets up before light to keep it in order. {He} does not ask you about it. But you see how they look at the well, and at the house, and at you with your dry cuffs, and old Mak from the mill has brought a chicken, and Mak is holding it out to nobody in particular.

choices.text: Take the chicken, and thank Mak, and do the pouring yourself

effects.log: You pour. You are bad at it. The old man looks at the gourd and at you. "Thank you," you say, and "it is a hard year," as you have heard it done, and the old man nods. You have the whole line done by noon, and your arm hurts, and it is a wonderful feeling.

choices.text: Let them bring what they like. It is only right

effects.log: By the next dry year there is a little roof over the well, and a stone. {npc} takes the chicken back to old Mak in person, and {he} does not speak to you until the rain.

events.text: It is the wrong end of a hot night, and you have stopped at the rim. Behind you {npc} has got to thirty, and has stopped. {He} does not start again. You can hear {him} breathing, with {his} back to you. "It is only," {he} says, to the wall. "Mun-seok's wife says that anyone would look. I said so too. I said anyone would." The bucket rope creaks. You are already half out of your hands.

choices.text: Come back up. Sit down. Tell {him} what is at the bottom, in words

effects.log: You tell {him}, with your back to the well. Length, teeth, weather. {He} listens to it all. "Well," {he} says, "I knew that you did not do a great deal around the house." And {he} goes back to thirty, and turns round to do it.

choices.text: Say only, "Thirty-one," and go down

effects.log: After a time, faintly, you hear it come after you: thirty-one. So that is all right. It is a very long while before it is really all right, and neither of you ever brings it up.

choices.text: Go down, and do not come up again. Better now, while it is still only a question

effects.log: You are at the bottom before {he} has turned round. A hundred is a long way to count, for someone who has nobody coming back. You do not know how far {he} goes, this time. You make sure not to listen.

events.text: You know before you know. You are well into the going, the shape coming off you in long wet ribbons and the horns not yet in, when the small round sky at the top of the well gets smaller. There is a face in it. {npc} is holding the lamp out behind {him}, so that it will not be seen. {His} hair has gone grey at the front. {He} is not suspicious at all. {He} only wanted to see you go, once, before {he} cannot.

choices.text: Go. The old law is the old law, and nobody ever came back up from this

effects.log: You go up past {him} in a column of black water, all of you, and the wall of the house goes, and you do not look. It is what the woman did, in the old story. They have that part right. You had not been told how quiet it would be after.

choices.text: Stop. Let the whole of you turn in the well and look back up

effects.log: You look at each other for as long as it lasts. It takes a while for something your size to turn. {He} does not drop the lamp. "So that is what you were doing," {he} says at last, and {his} voice shakes, and {he} goes in, and you hear {him} sit down. No law has ever covered what comes next.

choices.text: Go on down, as if you had not seen. Come up on the fifth evening, and let {him} count

effects.log: {He} counts. {He} counts very carefully, right to the end, on the fifth evening and every fifth evening after that. You both know. You have never been so polite to anyone in all your life.

events.text: It rains for three days, out of season, on one village, and the yard well rises by a hand, and that is when you know. They put {bk_child} in your arms, red and furious. It wants something. {npc} says, from the bed, that it is hungry and thirsty, and that it will be again shortly. You have been told about this. You stand and hold a thing that wants water with its entire body, and you own all of it, and it has no idea.

choices.text: Give it to {him}, and go and fetch what {he} needs yourself

effects.log: You go out to the well, and you take the yoke. Nobody has asked you to. You spill a good half of it on the way back, and {he} drinks what there is, and so, in a roundabout manner, does {bk_child}.

choices.text: Put one wet finger in its mouth

effects.log: It stops, and it stares at you. It sucks at the finger very hard, for some time, and then goes on screaming. You have been offered incense by whole dynasties, and you have never once been so flattered.

events.text: A second one, {bk_child}, and now there are two to get in out of the yard on the fifth evening. {npc} has a way of doing it. The big one is told to go and look at the hens, and the small one {he} holds with its face to {his} shoulder and {his} hand over the back of its head. Then {he} turns around, and {he} starts, out loud, counting for two. You stand at the rim with your hands empty. It looks like nothing at all.

choices.text: Go. That is what it is all for

effects.log: Going down, you can hear a very small voice trying it. It says one, and four, and another one. {npc} corrects it, and they start again. You have never in your life been so much in danger of being late.

choices.text: Stay for dinner, and go down late, and pay for it

effects.log: There is a storm in the south that comes three days behind, and people talk about it. You had a burnt bit of fish, and the small one got rice in your ear. You are not in the least sorry, and you are told that it shows.

events.text: {bk_child} is seven now, and has looked. Of course. You knew it on the way down, a small pair of eyes through small fingers. When you came up on the fifth evening, {bk_child} had been down the ladder to see, and came back up with one wet foot, entirely unimpressed. It is a well, you are informed. It smells. There is a frog. {bk_love} looks at you over that small head, and at the well, and then goes on shelling beans.

choices.text: Thank whoever wrote the law. It has no quarrel with this one

effects.log: It can look at anything it pleases for the rest of its life, and go in to dinner. You try to imagine that. You are glad, all that year, in a way that makes the rains somewhat absent-minded.

choices.text: Ask {bk_child} about the frog

effects.log: You are told a great deal about the frog. You nod. It is the longest talk that you have ever had with anyone on the subject of your home, and {bk_child} thinks that you could stand to get out more.

events.text: The worst month of the dry year, and {bk_child}, who is seven, has been digging in the yard with a wooden spoon. For three days. The neighbours have come to laugh, then to stop laughing. On the third evening the spoon comes up dark. {bk_child} sits back, soaked to the elbows, with water rising in the little hole, and looks round at {bk_love} with great seriousness. "You have to turn your back now," says {bk_child}.

choices.text: Watch {bk_love} turn. Listen to it start: one, two

effects.log: {bk_love} is crying and counting, and getting it wrong. You had thought the blood would frighten you. You stand in the yard, with your cuffs for once quite wet, and you turn your back too, and you count, because it is only manners.

choices.text: Fill that hole in by morning, and take the spoon away. It is so small

effects.log: You do it yourself, by night, and you put the spoon on the shelf. {bk_child} looks at the place in the yard, and at the shelf, and at you, and does not say anything. There are other spoons. You can feel the ground under that yard, waiting.

events.text: {npc} cannot get to the yard any more, so {he} does it from the mat, through the open door, with {his} face to the wall. {He} gets to about forty and goes to sleep. You have been waiting at the rim, with the hour going by. There are a great many things you have stopped pretending about. You go in and you sit down by {him}, and {he} opens one eye. You have been meaning to say this for a long time.

choices.text: "You can look now, if you want. I do not think that it matters"

effects.log: {He} thinks about it. It takes a while. "No," {he} says. "A bargain is a bargain, and I know what you look like." {He} turns {his} face to the wall. "Forty-one," {he} says. You go. You have held up the sky over three provinces, and you could not have said why you are shaking.

choices.text: Say nothing. Wait until {he} wakes, and go down on forty-one

effects.log: So it takes you four days to go home, that spring, and the rains are late, and the county builds you again. You can hear them shouting at the thing as far off as the east gate. {He} wakes up at dusk. "Forty-one," {he} says.

events.text: They carry {bk_love} up the hill on a clean bright morning, with the whole county walking behind and every one of the wells in the east scrubbed. Somebody did that. You stand in the yard when it is over, and your cuffs are dry, and the fifth evening comes the same as any. You go to the rim and put your hand on it. You have got into the way of waiting to go. There is no sound behind you of any kind.

choices.text: Say it yourself, out loud, the whole hundred, and go down

effects.log: You make a poor job of it. You go wrong around sixty, for no reason. It is dark by the time you are done, and an old neighbour has come to the wall to hear, and has turned her back.

choices.text: Do not go down. Stand there and let the rain come, for as long as it comes

effects.log: It comes for nineteen days, soft, without any wind. It does not do a thing to the crops. They say in the east that it was the best year that anyone remembers, and they say it very quietly.

events.text: Three provinces, some eighty years later, and you have got into the way of looking in on them. There is a family out by the east road who cannot see a guest off. Everyone knows that about them. The guest goes to the gate, and the entire house gets up, and turns to face the wall, and stands there in a row, grandmothers and all, until the gate shuts. They think it is good manners. It costs them a marriage now and then.

choices.text: Give them a good year, on the quiet

effects.log: The rice comes in early on that side of the road. They put it down to the well. They have a very good opinion of the well, and they cannot say why they keep it so clean.

choices.text: Leave them to it. Go by, at night, and do not stop

effects.log: You go by. Nobody looks. Not one of them, not even the children. It is a fine thing to be able to pass a house like that with your whole length in the air.

events.text: A dry county far from anyone you know. It is past midnight, and there is a person in the yard of the magistrate's office, with a good sword and a bad cough, and all the look of {bk_child}'s people, digging with a soup spoon. They have been at it since supper. They have no idea why. You can see them stop now and then, and look at the spoon, and curse it, and go on. You lie out along the sky with your eyes half shut.

choices.text: Send it up to them. It is the least you can do

effects.log: It comes up on the third night, cold and clean. The county is very grateful. By the end of the year they have put a stone up, saying a great many things about the magistrate, and none of them is true.

choices.text: Let them find it, or not. They had better learn that it is heavy

effects.log: They find it on the eleventh night, with their own arms, a long way down. Their hands will never be right again. You think they may be the first of that line who can tell you what water weighs.

events.text: You did not mean to come up that well. {npc} digs them for a living, a loud old person with a bad back, and {he} has dug straight into your road and is sitting at the bottom eating a pear. {He} looks you up and down. "Dry," {he} says. "My grandfather said there were some of you." You ask {him} whether, if it ever came to it, {he} would turn {his} back. "No," says {npc}. "I look at everything. It is my trade."

choices.text: Tell {him} all of it. Then see what {he} does when you go

effects.log: You tell it. {He} finishes the pear. And when you go, {he} sits there with {his} chin on {his} fist and watches every bit of it, and {he} is at the rim on the fifth evening with another pear. It seems that the law has nothing to say to a person who was told.

choices.text: Laugh, and go back the way you came

effects.log: You go up, and round, and home by the sea, which takes a week. You are old enough to know better, and you know better. You wonder for some time what kind of a pear that was.

events.text: A traveller has come up your valley, and has stopped by your water, facing the other way. They have put down their pack, and they keep their back to you the entire time, as if that were the natural way to call on anyone. "I was told never to look," they say to the hill. "I was told that it is only manners. I did want you to know that it has been kept." And they begin to count, in a good clear voice.

choices.text: Come up, all of you, behind them, while they count

effects.log: You rise the whole length, and you stand on the air at their back and let your shadow go over them. They get to a hundred without one mistake. They pick up their pack, and they bow to the hill, and they go.

choices.text: Lay a small rain down on their road, as far as the county line

effects.log: They go off with their collar up. You can see them, for a long way, walking in the only rain in the province, and they never once turn around to see where it is coming from.

events.text: You are six, and an aunt is going home. The aunt goes down the path with a bundle, and you stand and wave and watch all the way to the bend, because you like the aunt. Then you look round. The whole house has got up, and they are facing the wall. Somebody hisses at you. {npc}, who is not even of the family, reaches out without turning and takes you by the ear, and turns you round too.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Ask why, there and then, loudly

effects.log: "Because it is only manners," says {npc} to the wall. Nobody else in the district has these manners, you point out. "No," {npc} says. You are six, and you can tell a door when it has closed. You keep it in mind.

choices.text: Do it with the others, next time, and peep

effects.log: You get good at it. The trick is in the eyes. You see a great many people go round that bend, and nothing whatever happens. You begin to wonder what it is that the family thinks you will see.

events.text: There is something wrong with the wind. You noticed it flying kites at the first full moon. It is always at your back. You walk east and it is behind you, and you turn round and walk west, and it comes around. Your hair is always blowing forward into your soup. The other children have started to stand beside you when there is a kite fight on, and {npc} has started to watch them doing it.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Win the kite fight. All of them

effects.log: You cut eleven lines and you lose not one. It is the best day of your life. You do hear what the Song boy's grandmother says, on the way home. {npc} takes your kite away for a while, and {he} does it quite gently.

choices.text: Let your line go slack, and lose like anyone

effects.log: You lose, on purpose, in a following wind, with everybody watching. It is very hard to do, and it makes you strangely tired. Your kite comes down in the Songs' yard, and it comes down facing you.

events.text: You put your arm through the bottom of a jar, at fourteen, and you are cut from the wrist to the elbow. {npc} binds it, and frowns, and looks at the ache you keep rubbing behind your shoulder. In the morning, when {he} takes off the cloth, it has closed, a thin pink line with a bloom on it like a new leaf. It is the first week of spring. {He} looks out at the plum, and back at your arm.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Show the others. This is the most interesting thing you have ever done

effects.log: You show them. The Song boy tries to pay you to do it again. It hurts just the same, you find, and you heal just as quickly, and {npc} tells you in a level voice that there will be other people interested too.

choices.text: Keep the cloth on for a month, and limp a little

effects.log: You keep it on, and complain, and let them give you the soft rice. {npc} rewinds it once a week with great care. {He} is an excellent liar, for somebody who has never once said anything untrue to you.

events.text: You are sixteen, out on the east road, when the first rain of the year comes, and you stop walking. It falls on everyone. It takes more trouble with you. Something behind your shoulders that has ached all your life lets go at once, and you are standing with your head back and your mouth open, and {npc} is there under a straw cape. "Come in," {he} says. "It is about time that you heard why we do not see people off."
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Come in, and hear why

effects.log: A well. A person who came up it dry. A rule with a number in it, a child called {bk_line}, and the one who went home and may not have stopped, {bk_anc}. So you have been facing that wall for a reason. You think about the aunt on the path, and how you waved.

choices.text: Stay out in it a while. You can hear about it later

effects.log: {npc} goes in without you. You stand there until you are cold, and you find that you can do that, be cold. It is a great comfort. You do not ask {him} about it for a very long time, and {he} does not offer.

events.text: A bad dry year, and the district has come to the yard with its pebbles. The family well has never failed. Nobody knows why, the family least of all, and {npc} is keeping the line straight with a stick. Then the headman comes up to you in person, sweating, with a spoon in hand. A good silver spoon. The headman's grandmother told of something once, and it would be a kindness if you came to dig at the headman's place.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Go and dig. It seems you can

effects.log: You dig for two days, feeling stupid, with half the village looking on. It comes up on the third day, cold, and they all cheer, and {npc} walks you home by the back lane and says that you will find that you are very popular now, and for how long.

choices.text: Lend the headman a shovel, and say that the trade has a shovel

effects.log: The headman takes it, looking at you. The headman digs, and gets a wet hole and a bad back. A decent old man, and not a word said. You see that spoon on the headman's table when you go to pay your dues, and you do not look at it.

events.text: The rains are late and they have built the straw dragon. They ask you to help carry it because you are lucky. It is a village thing, and it is a good day out, and you are holding up the second loop when they start in with the sticks. You feel it. It is not much. It is across your back, right behind the shoulders, each blow, and the old men have begun telling it what they think, and {npc} is looking at you closely.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Take it. Grin. Shout along with the rest

effects.log: You shout as loudly as anyone. You go home with stripes across your shoulders that nobody put there. {npc} rubs some oil in without comment. It is a very good rain, and you are the only one who is annoyed about it.

choices.text: Say something to them. It is lazy, is it?

effects.log: It comes out of you in a voice you did not know you had. Everybody stops. You are a young person, in a field, shouting at some old men on behalf of some straw. There is a far-off sound of thunder. It does not make it any better.

events.text: One of the old ones of the house has died, and the bier goes out through the gate, and the family gets up as it has always done and faces the wall. It is the only funeral in the district where nobody follows. The neighbours are at the gate, and they are appalled. The Song grandmother's grandson, a friend of yours for forty years, says in your ear that this is really too much. {npc} has not turned. Neither have you.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Tell the grandson why. All of it. Forty years is long enough

effects.log: The grandson listens with a back to the bier, since you have made the grandson turn. Not a word is believed. But the grandson comes and stands next to you at the wall, and at the next one, and at the one after that.

choices.text: Say that it is an old custom, and that it is nobody's business

effects.log: The grandson goes off rather stiffly. That is two families who will not be coming to anything. You stand there and you count, because you always do. You have never in your life got past sixty without a mistake, and you wonder who started that.

events.text: You have been married for years, and {npc} has only now said it. {He} says it to the bowl. "When I go to the market," {he} says. "You always get up. You turn your face away and you stand there. I saw you in the first year. I thought that you must be very tired of me." {He} has been going out of that gate for all this time, with that. It takes you a moment to get your breath.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Tell {him}. Start with the well

effects.log: It takes most of the night. {He} says nothing, and then {he} says a good deal. At the end {he} goes out to the gate in the dark and comes back in, to see, and you get up and turn your back, and {he} starts to laugh and does not stop for some time, and {he} has to wipe {his} eyes on your sleeve.

choices.text: Say that it is a family habit, that it means nothing, and watch {him} go tomorrow

effects.log: You stand at the gate in the morning with your face to the road and your whole back crawling. You watch {him} go, the whole way to the bend. Nothing happens. You feel as if you had kicked a shrine, and {he} waves.

events.text: You go out to the gate one morning, and you turn your back, as you do. When you come in again {npc} is sitting on the step and looking at you. "You go wrong around sixty," {he} says. {He} is quite small. It seems {he} has been watching you do this since {he} could stand, with great interest, from behind. {He} wants to know what is going to happen if anybody looks. {He} has looked. {He} seems rather disappointed.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Tell {him} what is at the bottom of it. Take {him} to the well

effects.log: You let {him} look. You hold {him} by the belt. {He} looks for some time at the small round dark. "It smells," {he} says, but {he} is whispering it. You feel the belt go tight in your hand, as if {he} were leaning on a wind.

choices.text: Say that it is only manners. Turn {him} round by the ear

effects.log: {He} goes round. {He} makes a face at the wall, you can tell from the ears. It was done to you, and you turned out well enough, as far as anyone can see from where you are standing.

events.text: {npc} walks into the dry county with a forked willow stick and nothing else. {He} finds wells. {He} has found three this month, for a sack of rice each, and {he} has a very tired kind face. {He} comes down the market behind that stick, and stops at the salt stall, and the fork goes down in {his} hands so hard that it bends, and it is pointing at your stomach. {He} starts to laugh. "Oh, good," {he} says.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Take the stick away from {him}, and make your point

ok.log: You break it across your knee, and you put {him} on the ground. {He} lies looking up at the sky, still smiling. "That is all right," {he} says. "They grow on any riverbank." The market has seen you do it, too.

fail.log: {He} has walked more roads than you have. You are on your back in the salt with your ribs on fire, and {he} is holding your wrist and feeling the pulse, thoughtfully. "Very cold," {he} says, and {he} lets you go, for now.

choices.text: Buy your salt. Say that it must be the stall that is damp

effects.log: {He} laughs some more. {He} tips {his} hat to the salt seller. "It must be," {he} says. {He} walks off, with that stick held rather low, and at the end of the row it swings back round to look at you.

events.text: {npc} has come to the house, by the front gate, grey, with the same stick. {He} sits on your step. "Eleven dead wells in Hwa county," {he} says. "I was born in the twelfth, and I am the only one of that village who is left. I have found you a hundred wells, and they go dry. It is said a cup of your blood, in a dead well, will fill it for good." {He} is not threatening you. {He} has brought a cup. It is very clean.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: No. Not one drop, and {he} will not be asking the next of them

ok.log: It is short. {He} was never much of a fighter, and {he} knew that. You carry {him} back to the road and you leave {him} there, with the cup. {He} does not get up for some time. You think about Hwa county all that year, in spite of yourself.

fail.log: {He} has been thinking for ten years about how to do this. {He} takes you with a small hooked knife, in the thick of the arm, and {he} gets a good half cup, and goes. It heals by morning. In the spring you hear of a town in Hwa county with very sweet water.

choices.text: Go with {him} to Hwa county, with a shovel. Dig them yourself

effects.log: It takes two summers. You get six of the eleven, with your own back. {He} carries the stick ahead of you and says little. On the last day, {he} throws the cup down the sixth well and listens for it. "It is not the same," {he} says. "It will do."

events.text: You wake in the blue hour, standing in the yard, with the well cover in your two hands. You have no idea how you got here. Your feet are dry on the wet stones. There is a very cold breath coming up out of the dark, and the ache behind your shoulders is pleasant. Behind you someone is saying, in a low voice, "twenty-six, twenty-seven." {npc} has heard you get up. {He} is facing the house.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Put one leg over the rim

effects.log: You go down as far as you can, on nothing. It is not far, this time, and you hear {him} get to a hundred above you, without any mistakes, as you come back up. {He} does not ask you, and you do not say. {He} has started to look very old.

choices.text: Put the cover back on, and go and tell {him} to stop

effects.log: You lay it down square. You have to use both hands, and you find that you are leaning on it. "Fifty," says {npc}, and turns round, and looks at the well and not at you. "You should get a heavier cover," {he} says. So you get one.

events.text: Spring has not come. It is the third month, and there is ice on the paddies, and the plum has not moved. The old people say that they have seen it late, but not like this. You know it. It is in your chest, a great held breath that has been there since you woke. It is only stopped somewhere about you, and you could walk up on the east ridge at dawn and let it out. {npc} has noticed that you are not breathing much.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Go up the ridge, and breathe out

effects.log: It goes from you like something leaving home. By noon the snow is running. The plum comes out in two days, all at once, on one side only. You come down feeling thin and light. They are planting, and they do not know, and that is the arrangement.

choices.text: Hold it. It is the sky's work, and you are a grain clerk's cousin

effects.log: It takes another three weeks to come by itself. It is a thin year. You are not to blame, and nobody says so. Your chest hurts until the summer, and there are fewer plums for everyone, and you know exactly how many.

events.text: {npc} takes you to the first well, the one that the family came from, in a walled yard at the east end of nowhere. It has no bucket. "Somebody ought to look," says {npc}. "After all this time. I do not suppose that it can leave twice." {He} walks over to the wall and turns {his} back, and {he} starts, one, two. You stand with both hands on the stone. It is very cold, and {bk_anc} is down there, what there is of it.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Look

effects.log: You lean out. There is a long dark, and a small round sky. Then, very far down, the dark has an eye, the size of a threshing floor, and it opens, and it looks at you with no surprise. It has been waiting for one of you to be rude. Your hands stop being afraid.

choices.text: Turn your back too, and count

effects.log: You face the wall, next to {npc}. At about sixty you go wrong, and something behind you rises out of the well without a sound. It goes on rising. The wind lifts your hair forward, and it is very gentle. You get all the way to a hundred. Nobody looks. When you turn, the moss is wet.

events.text: You go back, at the end of a dry spring. {npc} waits at the gate of the yard, too stiff for the rest of it. You sit down on the rim of the well, in the blue hour, and it takes a long time to start. It is coming up out of the dark, in a voice like water being carried. It is counting. It is {bk_anc}, and it is very slow. It gets as far as ninety-nine, and stops, and you wait, and it does not go on.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Say it. "A hundred"

effects.log: There is a silence, as long as a good rain. Then something gives a long breath, all the way up, and it smells of smoke. Somebody was owed that. You will never know how long it has waited, and you have a bad feeling that you do.

choices.text: Say nothing. It is not your number. Bow to the well, and go

effects.log: You leave it at ninety-nine. That is a thing it may want to keep. You have a bucket of that water, and {npc} drinks some at the gate, and {he} makes a face. "Dry," {he} says, and {he} laughs at that for most of the way home.

events.text: You are the only person in the county with no grey in your hair, and it has started to rain when you are annoyed. {npc} sits down with you on the rim. "You are looking both ways at once," {he} says. You could cap that well with stone, and be somebody who gets thirsty. You could go down it the whole way, with the family counting. There is another thing, {he} says, but only the very rude have tried it.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Cap it. Be thirsty

effects.log: You lay the last stone yourself, and it takes all of the summer. The ache behind your shoulders goes off, like a guest. That evening you are thirsty, and you stand in the yard for some time with your mouth a little open, working it out.

choices.text: Go down, and do not look back. They will not either

effects.log: You walk out into the yard at the blue hour, and you do not say anything. You hear the door. You hear them come out, and turn, the whole house, and somebody starts it off. You are at thirty before the shape comes off you.

choices.text: Go down on the fifth evening. Come up for dinner

effects.log: The old law says that whoever looks has lost you, and nobody thought to make a law about being hungry. {npc} remarks that somebody a long time back must have been very good about counting.

events.text: You have got a bad back, and you could not be happier. Every morning you take the yoke down to the well like everybody else, with your feet slipping, and you stop halfway, because your arms have given out. You drink like a horse. You had no idea. {npc} comes by and watches you pant. "So what is it like?" {he} says. You think of how to put it. You pour a dipper over your own head, and you groan.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Queue with the others, with a pebble, in the dry months

effects.log: You have a forty-three this year, and you stand in the sun and complain about the forty-twos. It is a good life. Somebody asks you whether it is going to rain, and you have to say that you could not tell them.

choices.text: Scrub the village well, this spring. It is your turn

effects.log: You go down the ladder, backwards, with the brush in your teeth. It is cold, and it stinks, and there is nobody down there. You scrub for most of the day. You come up as wet as anyone has ever been.

events.text: You come up on the old days, in the blue hour, when it can be managed. You have to think about the shape. Your cuffs are dry, and you sit down to dinner with people whose names you have been told, and everybody is careful about the soup. Then it is time. You get up, and go out, and behind you there is a long scrape as the entire table stands. Somebody small, {npc}, starts counting, and gets it wrong.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Stop on the rim, and hear it right to the end

effects.log: They do not miss a number now. There are thirty of them at it, and they sound like a school. You do not know who they think they are doing this for, and when they finish you are already long gone, and you are not.

choices.text: Send a good rain on them, in place of coming, in the years you cannot

effects.log: It falls on the one house first, each spring, for a little while, as a courtesy. They come out and stand in it. Then they go in, with their backs to you, and you take that as it was meant.

events.text: It is a strange arrangement. You are a dull person in a dull robe, who owes the mill for flour, and on the fifth evening you get up from the mat with a sigh, as you would to see about a leak. {npc} has given up on the whole thing. "Bring back some fish, if you are going by," {he} says, not looking up. You have put down a storm over the west coast with a sore tooth, and you got home in time for the end of the rice.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Hold off the rain until the peppers are in. They are your peppers

effects.log: You do. All the county's peppers come in very well as a result, and nobody knows that they owe it to one person's opinion of soup. There are worse ways for the sky to be run.

choices.text: Bring back the fish

effects.log: It is a very large one, of a kind that nobody can name. {npc} looks at it for some time, and asks if it was the only one you could get. You eat it for a week. You are not sure that you have ever been so well.

events.text: You are old, and you have taken to telling the small ones why the family does what it does. They want to know what would happen if somebody looked. You say that the one who looks loses the one who goes. They think that over. "But they would be gone anyway," says one of them. "That is what going is." {npc}, who has brought the tea, looks at you sidelong. Nobody has made that point in several hundred years.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Tell them that they may look, if they want, when you go

effects.log: They are horrified. They would not dream of it. It is only manners. You have tried, at least, and you sit there and you drink your tea and you are enormously pleased with all of them.

choices.text: Tell them that they have the number wrong, too. It was about a hundred

effects.log: That starts it. Is it a hundred, or about a hundred? They are at it for the whole of the winter. Two cousins stop speaking. It is the first new idea that the family has had, and you feel that you have left something behind.

events.text: It is the first warm evening of the year, and you know quite well what kind of evening it is. They have brought you out to the step, in a blanket. The whole house is there, and there are a great many, and {npc} keeps looking at the sky. You have spent your whole life facing a wall. You have seen a thousand backs. You find there is one thing you would have liked, and you have never said it to anyone.
events.arc: The Family That Turns Its Back

choices.text: Ask one of them to stay facing you, and look

effects.log: They do not want to. It is the smallest one who comes up in the end, and sits down in front of you, and stares very hard, as if at a difficult sum. You have never been so looked at. The wind comes round behind you, the way it does.

choices.text: Say nothing. Hear them get up, and begin

effects.log: There is a long scrape as they rise. You hear them turn. It starts up from somewhere in the back, ragged, one, two, and they all come in. It is a good sound. You have wondered for years what it was like from this end.
